transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (AE), Marco Chen (SE), Elena Ruiz (Enablement), Priya Nair (PMM), Sam Ortiz (Sales), Zoe Park (SE trainee), NA Sales group

Summary:
Internal SE/AE enablement focused on unified messaging for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, competitive positioning vs major API vendors, and live demo practice with common customer objections. Quick agreement on next steps: update battle cards, record short demo snippets, schedule follow-up role-play.

Topics:
- Core pitch: performance + cost controls + unified API across deployment modes
- Competitive differentiators: fallbacks, routing, cost-aware batching, observability
- Demo flow: 1) quick intro & qualification, 2) live example (chat & embeddings), 3) show console metrics + rollout controls, 4) handle objections (latency vs cost, security)
- Role-play scenarios and feedback

Transcript:
00:00 Jasmine (AE): okay folks, thanks for joining, we'll kick this off, plan is 60 minutes, short messaging refresh and then demo practice, Elena I'll hand it over to you to start the framing
00:12 Elena (Enablement): cool thanks, um, high level goal is consistent language so the customer hears the same thing from AE and SE, we get asked the same questions about Dedicated vs Hosted and private deploys so we want the crisp 30-second pitch
00:30 Priya (PMM): quick note, we've updated the battle card with the new quantization line, but it's still a draft, so don't quote exact numbers, say "quantization profiles" and "recommendations"
00:45 Marco (SE): for the technical opening I like lead with predictability: "We help you run inference with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments" then back it up with examples, like autoscaling for Dedicated and KMS integration for Private
01:10 Sam (Sales): a question that keeps coming up - customers ask why not just call OpenAI for hosted, how do we frame the Cost vs Turnkey tradeoff?
01:25 Jasmine (AE): I usually say: OpenAI gives you a great hosted API but we give you predictable unit economics and routing controls; you can start hosted then pin to Dedicated with minimal code changes. emphasize "same API, different deployment"
01:45 Zoe (SE trainee): is there a short line on fallbacks? sometimes customers worry about SLA, what do we say?
01:55 Marco (SE): fallback messaging: "we offer automated routing and model variants so if a region or variant is congested we fall back to compatible options - this keeps apps online while preserving cost targets" - maybe shorter: "automated fallbacks to keep you online"
02:18 Priya (PMM): competitor note, don't call it "fallbacks" with certain customers, call it "automated routing and graded model variants" which sounds less like degraded experience
02:40 Jasmine (AE): ok demo flow, Marco you'll show a short live chat then flip to console to show latency and token cost breakdowns, then show rollout controls and a canary example, then we hit an objection role-play
03:00 Marco (SE): got it, I'll start with a 2-turn chat using the hosted endpoint, then show switching to Dedicated, quick change in config and no client-side change, then show console with token-level breakdown and route policy
03:22 Elena (Enablement): remember to narrate what the customer cares about - e.g., "this is what reduces your per-token cost" instead of kernel-level detail about quantization unless they ask
03:40 Sam (Sales): practice objection now - I'll play a procurement lead, skeptical about on-prem, cost, timeline
03:50 Jasmine (AE): perfect, I'll play the customer, Marco you be SE, Zoe observe and give feedback
04:05 Role-play start
04:10 Sam (Procurement - role): We're concerned about time to provision Dedicated GPUs and complexity for KMS, why take Redwood vs just using managed endpoints elsewhere?
04:25 Marco (SE): yeah totally, so a couple points, we offer reserved Dedicated pools with autoscaling policies so you get predictable throughput and capacity commits, and for KMS we have integrations with common providers - most setups take X to Y weeks depending on approvals
04:40 Sam (Procurement - role): X to Y weeks sounds vague, they ask for specifics, can you guarantee timelines?
04:50 Marco (SE): I should avoid exact weeks in enablement, better to say "typical setup varies - small pilots can be up in days, larger enterprise setups with KMS and VPCs often take a few weeks with legal approvals" - then commit to a post-call technical checklist
05:10 Jasmine (AE): good correction, we need that checklist as an artifact to send, that's an action item
05:20 Zoe (Observer): feedback - Marco was good but used "reserved Dedicated pools" which sometimes confuses non-technical buyers, maybe say "dedicated capacity that you reserve"
05:35 Marco (SE): noted, rephrase: "dedicated capacity you reserve for predictable throughput"
05:50 Priya (PMM): quick competitive note: when OpenAI is mentioned, avoid bashing; instead say "they're a great hosted option; our differentiation is predictable economics, deployment flexibility, and observability for production apps"
06:10 Jasmine (AE): let's go through the demo script step by step, Marco start the chat and narrate the customer's mental model
06:30 Marco (SE): typing - "Hello Redwood, we have a multi-tenant chat application, users expect sub-300ms latency for short prompts, and logs must be auditable", then show a response, then show switching model variant to a quantized lower-cost variant
06:58 (Demo glitch) Marco (SE): hmm screen share lag, sorry, give me a sec - these practice demos always have the network gremlins
07:20 Marco (SE): ok back, live response: "Sure, You can set routing rules to prefer low-latency endpoints for short prompts and fallback to cost-optimized routes for batch jobs" - note transcription has "KV cash" earlier in docs, should be "KV cache"
07:45 Elena (Enablement): make sure to explain prefix caching: say "we cache repeated prefixes and KV cache to speed up repeated user conversations" not "KV cash" cause that confuses folks
08:05 Sam (Sales): a frequent objection - what about quantization harming quality? customers worry about hallucinations rising when you quantize a model
08:20 Marco (SE): answer: "we provide quantization profiles and recommendations per workload; we run a brief eval against your prompt set to validate quality before recommending a quantized variant" - good line: "evaluation-driven quantization"
08:45 Zoe (SE trainee): note the word recommendations is actually recommendations - small transcribe error but keep language tight
09:00 Priya (PMM): let's practice the 30-second pitch now, take turns
09:05 Jasmine (AE): 30-sec pitch: "Redwood Inference provides a single API to run models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help teams get predictable latency and cost, with routing, caching, and rollout controls built-in so your app stays online during spikes."
09:30 Marco (SE): alternate: "We enable cost-aware inference: automatic batching, KV cache and model quantization recommendations, plus a runtime that picks optimized kernels for your infra so you get predictable performance"
09:55 Elena (Enablement): feedback - good, Marco try to remove "kernels" for non-technical buyers, use "optimized execution"
10:10 Role-play 2: Sales objection around compliance
10:20 Sam (Security role): we're in regulated finance, need SOC2 + audit logs, how does Redwood help?
10:30 Marco (SE): we support SOC2 controls, KMS integration, audit logs and private deployment options (VPC, on-prem) - recommend we offer Private for fully isolated setups
10:50 Sam (Security role): what about attestation and third-party audits?
11:00 Jasmine (AE): we can provide SOC2 report and our compliance package; action: send security docs link post-call
11:10 Priya (PMM): tag - include a short note on data residency for customers that ask about EU/GDPR
11:30 Elena (Enablement): demo - flip to console, show cost breakdown view; Marco narrate what the customer sees: token-level cost and route cost per model version
11:50 Marco (SE): showing console now, note: the console example is synthetic for the demo, real numbers will differ, and the token breakdown shows how caching reduced per-token cost by ~30% on this test workload
12:20 Jasmine (AE): good callout to not overpromise exact numbers, use ranges or say "typical"
12:35 Role-play - procurement pushes on pricing
12:45 Sam (Procurement): your price per commit seems higher than our current provider, how do you justify?
12:55 Marco (SE): justify with unit economics - lower tail-latency, fewer retries, improved cache hit rates, and the ability to route workloads to cheaper variants when acceptable - basically total cost of ownership
13:20 Priya (PMM): recommend calling out "cost controls" as a core feature set - not just "we're cheaper" but "we help you control where spend goes"
13:45 Elena (Enablement): quick feedback round - Zoe, what's one improvement for Marco's demo presence?
13:50 Zoe (SE trainee): speak slower, label steps for the audience, e.g., "Step 1: set routing rule" then pause to let them read the console
14:05 Marco (SE): noted, will add explicit step labels to the script
14:20 Jasmine (AE): we'll record a short 30-second clip of the switch from hosted to dedicated to share with AEs, that's in the next steps
14:35 Sam (Sales): can we get a one-pager on migration path and a checklist for pilots?
14:45 Jasmine (AE): yes that's an action item - checklist + pilot runbook
15:00 Elena (Enablement): now let's do one tricky scenario: customer cares only about latency and is worried cost will explode if we push for redundancy
15:10 Role-play start
15:15 Sam (Latency role): we need sub-200ms 95th percentile for chat; how do you prove you can do that at scale?
15:30 Marco (SE): short answer: we can run a benchmark using your prompts and traffic profile; we also support kernel selection and optimized runtimes - and show console traces for p95 - commit to run a pilot benchmark
15:50 Sam (Latency role): they ask about network hops and region selection
16:00 Marco (SE): answer: we support regional routing and colocated endpoints; use regional fallbacks for availability while preferring low-latency hops
16:20 Jasmine (AE): callout: avoid saying "we guarantee" unless there's an SLA - reference SLA only when contractually available
16:40 Priya (PMM): competitive quickfire - how to position vs Anthropic?
16:50 Marco (SE): say: "Anthropic provides strong safety-first models; our angle is production-grade serving and operational tooling that helps you ship at scale"
17:05 Priya (PMM): vs OpenAI?
17:10 Jasmine (AE): "OpenAI is great for quick dev velocity; we offer same API ergonomics plus routing, dedicated capacity, and observability for production apps"
17:30 Elena (Enablement): back to demo scripts - Marco, run through the actual script verbatim while we time it for <8 minutes total
17:45 Marco (SE): starting script: 1) intro and qualification (1 min), 2) demo chat hosted (2 min), 3) switch to dedicated and show console (2 min), 4) rollout and canary (1 min), 5) wrap up and next steps (1 min)
18:10 (Timing note) Zoe (Observer): that looks like 7 minutes, good, but leave buffer for questions
18:25 Jasmine (AE): practice makes perfect, let's do a full timed run, Elena you time, Priya provide competitive objections
18:40 Timed run begins
18:50 Marco (SE): intro: "Hi I'm Marco, SE at Redwood, quick question: are you primarily latency or cost driven?"
19:10 Jasmine (AE): very good opener, short and qualifying
19:30 Marco (SE): demo hosted chat, quick response shown, then switch config to Dedicated - share screen shows no client changes, just toggle route policy
20:00 (Demo note) Marco (SE): console shows p95 trace and token-level cost, briefly explain caching effect
20:30 Priya (PMM): objection: "what about vendor lock-in?"
20:40 Marco (SE): answer: "we keep your app code stable; you can change underlying models or deployment modes without changing API calls"
21:00 Jasmine (AE): end of timed demo, feedback: stronger vocal transitions between steps, call out what the audience should be looking at on the console
21:20 Elena (Enablement): final feedback round: common mistakes - overuse of jargon, premature deep dives, committing to timelines without checklist
21:40 Action recap:
- share one-pager and battle card (Jasmine / Priya)
- record short demo clip (Marco)
- pilot checklist + security docs (SE / AE)
22:05 Closing remarks
22:10 Jasmine (AE): great session everyone thanks, we'll follow-up with recordings and the artifacts, see calendar invite for follow-up role-play next week
22:20 End
